subject.title: [Analysis] Identify performance bottlenecks in native OpenClaw setup on constrained VPS

question: What native-Linux VPS measurement environment, layer scope, and acceptance criteria should issue #53600 use before any docs runbook or fix PR is queued?
rationale: The repository already has multiple telemetry primitives, so the remaining choice is which host/profile and which layer-attribution evidence maintainers consider sufficient rather than a deterministic one-file repair.

options.title: Scope a measured runbook
options.body: Use one maintainer-approved Linux VPS profile and existing telemetry first, then file narrow follow-up PRs only for proven instrumentation gaps.

options.title: Split by subsystem
options.body: Convert this broad request into separate issues for context assembly, memory search, compaction, Telegram delivery, auth/fallback, and embedded-runner prep.

options.title: Close as support tuning

recommendation.body: Use one maintainer-approved Linux VPS profile and existing telemetry first, then file narrow follow-up PRs only for proven instrumentation gaps.
